title: Fold it or spread it?
hook: Fold it or spread it: does that change how long a towel takes to dry?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that water leaves cloth only through the surface open to the air, so a towel folded in quarters shows about a quarter of that surface and dries several times slower than the same towel spread flat

misconception: Folding a towel doesn't change how fast it dries, because the same water has to leave either way.
objective: Spreading the towel exposes both large faces. This constant-rate model divides water mass by exposed area and assumed flux; a smaller evaporation doorway gives a longer model time.

claims.text: Spreading the towel opens both large faces to the air. In this model each square metre of open face dries at the same speed, so the time falls as the open face grows.
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/13-6-humidity-evaporation-and-boiling (opened 2026-10-14). Evaporation is inhibited by humidity. The card's constant flux is an explicitly illustrative assumption, not a measured household drying rate. In this model the folded towel shows 2·W·1.4/4 m² and the spread towel 2·W·1.4 m², and time = 0.6/(area × 0.102) at a constant flux per m², so time falls as open face grows (12 h → 3 h at W = 70). The physical part ('water leaves through the face open to the air') is consistent with OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, opened 2026-10-16 as the book's CNXML source (github.com/openstax/osbooks-college-physics-bundle, modules/m42219/index.cnxml via raw.githubusercontent.com, sha256 4d622c5f94e2…; openstax.org itself is blocked here): evaporation happens at the liquid surface while the air is below saturation.

claims.text: Real drying depends on fabric, temperature, humidity and airflow; this is not a twelve-hour promise.

recall.question: Same water, same air: layout A has 1 m² of face open to the air and layout B has 2 m². How do their drying times compare in this model?
recall.why: In this model each square metre of open face dries at the same speed, so time = water ÷ (open face × that speed). Doubling the open face halves the time. This does not promise a real household drying-time ratio.
